description: STACKIT-specific architecture for a hybrid (on-prem + STACKIT) Kubernetes platform: services, SKE/Gardener, networking (SNA, VPN), identity and secrets, tenancy and DR, and central management from the on-prem DC. Generic GitOps/fleet concepts live in the Platform Engineering deck.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: Who operates STACKIT, and why do architects choose it?
notes.back: The Schwarz Group (Lidl, Kaufland). Main reason: digital sovereignty — EU data residency, General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) alignment, no exposure to the US CLOUD Act.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: Where are STACKIT's data centers, and what is its primary region?
notes.back: Only in Germany and Austria. Primary region eu01 with availability zones eu01-1/2/3.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: Which open-source stack is STACKIT's IaaS layer built on?
notes.back: OpenStack (e.g. Cinder block storage behind STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) volumes).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.text: STACKIT resource hierarchy: {{c1::Organization}} → {{c2::Folder(s)}} → {{c3::Project}}; role assignments inherit downward.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: What is a STACKIT Project the unit of?
notes.back: Resource ownership, identity and access management (IAM) role assignment, quotas and billing attribution — roughly a GCP project.
notes.extra: Landing-zone practice: one project per team × environment (e.g. payments-dev, payments-prod).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: Which identity types exist in STACKIT identity and access management (IAM), and where are roles granted?
notes.back: User accounts (portal login) and project-scoped service accounts (machines), granted roles (owner, editor, reader, service-specific) on organization, folder or project.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.text: STACKIT management interfaces: the {{c1::Portal}} (web UI); the {{c2::STACKIT CLI}} (stackit, also a kubectl credential helper); {{c3::REST APIs + SDKs}} (Go, Python, Java, JS); the {{c4::Terraform provider}} stackitcloud/stackit (the infrastructure as code (IaC) standard).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.text: STACKIT compute: {{c1::Compute Engine}} = OpenStack VMs (≈ EC2); {{c2::STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE)}} = managed Kubernetes (≈ GKE/AKS/EKS); {{c3::Cloud Foundry}} = PaaS for pushing apps without managing clusters; {{c4::Confidential Server / Confidential Kubernetes}} = in-memory-encrypted compute for highly sensitive workloads.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.text: STACKIT managed data services: databases {{c1::PostgreSQL Flex}}, MongoDB Flex, SQL Server Flex, MariaDB; cache {{c2::Redis}}; search and log analytics {{c3::OpenSearch}}; messaging {{c4::RabbitMQ}} and PubSub.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.text: STACKIT storage → Kubernetes: {{c1::Block Storage}} (Cinder) → ReadWriteOnce (RWO) PersistentVolumes; {{c2::File storage / NFS shares}} → ReadWriteMany (RWX) volumes; {{c3::Object Storage}} (S3-compatible) → backups, Terraform state, Loki chunks; {{c4::Backup Storage}} → cost-optimised, geo-redundant target for volume backups.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.text: STACKIT security & dev tooling: {{c1::Secrets Manager}} (managed secret storage/rotation); {{c2::KMS}} (key operations, envelope encryption); {{c3::Container Registry}} (private OCI registry with vulnerability scanning); {{c4::STACKIT Git}} (managed repos); {{c5::Run Command}} (scripts on VMs without SSH).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: What is STACKIT Observability built on, and what was its old name?
notes.back: Managed Prometheus, Grafana, Loki and Tempo (metrics, logs, traces, alerting). Formerly Argus — that name is deprecated.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: STACKIT LogMe vs Telemetry Router?
notes.back:
Logs/LogMe: centralized log ingestion, storage and search.
Telemetry Router: central handling of audit streams.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.text: STACKIT networking: {{c1::STACKIT Network Area (SNA)}} — org-level private network joining projects, the hybrid hub; {{c2::VPN}} — managed Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) site-to-site into the SNA; {{c3::Network / Application Load Balancer}} — L4 / L7 (web application firewall (WAF) option); {{c4::Unified Firewall}} — central rules across projects (beta).
notes.extra: Also: DNS (hosted zones, works with external-dns), Security Groups (stateful instance firewalls), content delivery network (CDN).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: Why is STACKIT attractive for Dutch/EU public-sector compliance (Baseline Informatiebeveiliging Overheid 2 (BIO2), Network and Information Security Directive 2 (NIS2))?
notes.back: EU-only data residency (DE/AT), General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) alignment, no US CLOUD Act exposure, ISO 27001 and BSI C5 attestations.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::01 STACKIT Foundations
notes.front: Running Baseline Informatiebeveiliging Overheid 2 (BIO2)/Network and Information Security Directive 2 (NIS2) workloads on STACKIT: what remains your job (shared responsibility)?
notes.back: Zoning/segmentation, access control and joiner-mover-leaver via your Active Directory (AD), central audit logging, encryption config, incident response, and demonstrable control of the deployment chain (GitOps + signed images).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Which open-source project is STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) built on?
notes.back: Gardener (open-sourced by SAP): manages fleets of Kubernetes clusters using Kubernetes itself.
notes.extra: STACKIT operates the control planes; clusters are self-service via Portal, CLI, API or Terraform, with auto-updates and auto-repair. Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)-conformant.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.text: Gardener model: the {{c1::Garden}} cluster runs Gardener itself; {{c2::Seed}} clusters host customer control planes (apiserver, etcd) as pods; a {{c3::Shoot}} is your cluster — control plane in a STACKIT seed, only the worker nodes run as VMs in your project.
notes.analogy: Kubernetes running Kubernetes: seeds are nurseries where the provider tends every shoot's control plane; you only see the leaves — the worker nodes.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) shoot model: what can't you touch, and what is STACKIT's job as a result?
notes.back: You never see or SSH the control plane; its scaling, high availability (HA) and etcd backups are STACKIT's job.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.text: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) node pool settings: machine {{c1::flavor}} (e.g. g1.3); {{c2::min/max node count}} for autoscaling; {{c3::availability zones}} (eu01-1/2/3); boot volume size/type; {{c4::labels and taints}} for workload placement.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Which OS do STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) nodes run, and what does that imply for operations?
notes.back: Flatcar Container Linux — immutable and auto-updating: treat nodes as replaceable, don't hand-tune them.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Why run several node pools in one STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) cluster?
notes.back: To separate system, tenant and GPU workloads with different flavors, taints and scaling limits.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: How does STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) apply Kubernetes patch and Flatcar OS updates?
notes.back: Automatically, inside a configurable maintenance window.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: What happens when a STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) cluster's Kubernetes minor version leaves support?
notes.back: It is force-upgraded — you can't pin a version forever.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: How should you plan around STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) auto-updates across a fleet?
notes.back: Stagger maintenance windows by ring (canary first), keep PodDisruptionBudgets correct so drains don't take services down, and test API deprecations continuously.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: What is STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) cluster hibernation?
notes.back: A scheduled shutdown of the cluster (control plane and workers scaled to zero), e.g. dev/test clusters off nights and weekends.
notes.analogy: Switching off office lights and heating at weekends: big savings, but Monday morning needs a moment to warm up.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) hibernation: trade-off, and what does it enable for tenancy?
notes.back: Wake-up latency — unusable for anything serving traffic or running jobs. But it makes cluster-per-team affordable for dev.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: What do you pay for with STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE)?
notes.back: A per-cluster fee for the managed control plane, plus normal Compute Engine, storage and load balancer (LB) prices for the workers.
notes.extra: Tenancy consequence: per-cluster fees make "a cluster for everyone" costlier than namespaces — quantify it in the tenancy decision.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Which two levers cut STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) non-production spend?
notes.back: Hibernation schedules for dev/test clusters, and autoscaling node pools with low minimums and right-sized flavors.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.text: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) autoscaling layers: nodes — {{c1::Cluster Autoscaler}} per node pool within min/max; pods — {{c2::HPA and VPA}}; event-driven — {{c3::KEDA}} (e.g. on queue depth).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Why is a STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) node pool's max size also a tenancy control?
notes.back: A runaway tenant can only grow to the pool max — the autoscaler limit acts as a hard compute quota.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) admin kubeconfig: what is it, and why treat it as break-glass only?
notes.back: Client-certificate based, valid up to 180 days, with coarse revocation: rotating credentials invalidates all admin kubeconfigs and ServiceAccount tokens. Store it offline.
notes.analogy: A master key without per-copy revocation: change the lock and every copy — plus every ServiceAccount key — stops working.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Default way for operators to get STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) credentials?
notes.back: stackit ske kubeconfig login as a kubectl exec plugin: fetches short-lived credentials on demand via your STACKIT identity.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE)'s STACKIT identity provider (IDP) integration: what does it do, and what's its gap?
notes.back: Per cluster, users log in with STACKIT accounts and RBAC binds to their email addresses. It doesn't speak your corporate Active Directory (AD) — hence PingFederate/Pinniped designs.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: What does a type: LoadBalancer Service create on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE)?
notes.back: The cloud controller manager provisions a STACKIT Network Load Balancer (L4 TCP/UDP) with a public IP, billed in your project.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: How do you expose a STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) Service only to on-prem over the virtual private network (VPN)?
notes.back: The internal load balancer (LB) annotation: the LB gets a private IP in the node network instead of a public one.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE): what does spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges do, and what's the gotcha?
notes.back: A classless inter-domain routing (CIDR) allow-list of callers (add on-prem ranges). Include the pod CIDR if pods themselves must reach the load balancer (LB).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: How do you preserve client source IPs through a STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) load balancer?
notes.back: Enable PROXY protocol v2 via the lb.stackit.cloud/... annotation (the backend must speak it).
notes.analogy: A forwarding envelope that keeps the original sender's return address on the letter.
notes.extra: Source-IP session persistence is also available by annotation.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) persistent volumes: what backs them, and what constraints follow?
notes.back: A Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver on Cinder block storage: StorageClasses per performance tier, ReadWriteOnce (RWO) only, zone-bound volumes → StatefulSets must respect zones.
notes.extra: ReadWriteMany (RWX) needs the Network File System (NFS)/file-storage offering.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: How do you back up STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) volumes?
notes.back: Container Storage Interface (CSI) volume snapshots + Velero, writing to STACKIT Object Storage.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: For multi-cluster or disaster recovery (DR) on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE), why prefer managed databases (DBs) and Object Storage over cluster volumes?
notes.back: Block storage doesn't replicate across clusters; managed services survive cluster loss and are reachable from any cluster.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) default network posture: worker nodes vs API server?
notes.back: Nodes are private (no public IPs; inbound only via load balancers (LBs), outbound via provider network address translation (NAT)). The kube-apiserver endpoint is public by default — it lives in the STACKIT seed.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: How do you harden access to the STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) API server?
notes.back: Enable the access control list (ACL) extension to allow-list only your on-prem egress IPs/virtual private network (VPN) ranges, use short-lived credentials (stackit ske kubeconfig login), and audit tool identities separately.
notes.extra: Private API-server access options exist for callers inside the STACKIT network — verify the current options per cluster.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Where does STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) expose cluster metadata such as the pod classless inter-domain routing (CIDR)?
notes.back: In the shoot-info ConfigMap in kube-system.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.text: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) cluster extensions (e.g. toggled via Terraform): {{c1::observability}} wires the cluster to a STACKIT Observability instance (the old argus block is deprecated); {{c2::dns}} integrates STACKIT DNS; {{c3::acl}} allow-lists API-server access; {{c4::application_load_balancer}} gives managed L7 ingress.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Creating STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) and in-cluster resources in one Terraform run: how are credentials wired?
notes.back: stackit_ske_cluster creates the cluster; stackit_ske_kubeconfig (refresh = true) yields credentials fed into the kubernetes/helm providers.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: How can Terraform's kubernetes/helm providers authenticate to STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) without long-lived certs in state?
notes.back: Exec-plugin auth that calls stackit ske kubeconfig login.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Pitfalls of configuring Kubernetes from the same Terraform apply that creates STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) — and the better pattern?
notes.back: Kubeconfig material lands in state, and provider-in-same-apply ordering is fragile. Better: Terraform bootstraps only the GitOps agent; GitOps does the rest.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.text: Managed STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) still leaves you the day-2 stack: {{c1::ingress controller, cert-manager, external-dns}}; {{c2::GitOps agent and policy engine}}; {{c3::External Secrets Operator}}; {{c4::observability agents (Alloy/OTel) and Velero}}; plus registry credentials, image-signing policy, NetworkPolicies and quotas.
notes.analogy: SKE hands you a serviced building shell; furniture, alarm system and locks are still your job.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Why is the day-2 "golden stack" the real multi-cluster problem on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE)?
notes.back: It must be identical across the fleet, so it has to live in Git and be reconciled by GitOps — never hand-applied.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: NetworkPolicy on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE): what's the default, and what must the platform team ship?
notes.back: SKE's Container Network Interface (CNI) enforces standard NetworkPolicy, but Kubernetes defaults to allow-all. Ship default-deny ingress and egress per tenant namespace, with explicit allows (kube-dns, ingress controller).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::02 SKE Core
notes.front: Why avoid designing around Container Network Interface (CNI)-specific features on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE)?
notes.back: On a managed cluster you don't choose the CNI or its low-level config, so you can't guarantee those features fleet-wide.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Building blocks of a STACKIT Compute Engine VM?
notes.back: An OpenStack flavor (g1.x general purpose, compute/memory-optimised, GPU incl. NVIDIA A100) in an availability zone, a boot volume from an image plus data volumes, project networks, security groups, optional public IP.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Why do VMs still matter in a Kubernetes-centric STACKIT design?
notes.back: Virtual private network (VPN) test endpoints, jump hosts and self-managed appliances (e.g. self-run VPN gateways).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: How is STACKIT Block Storage tiered, and what are its key properties?
notes.back: Performance classes (e.g. storage_premium_perfX, input/output operations per second (IOPS) rising per class) chosen per volume or STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) StorageClass; volumes are zonal; snapshots and backups supported.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: How is access to STACKIT Object Storage granted?
notes.back: It's S3-compatible: credential groups issue access/secret keys scoped to buckets.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.text: STACKIT Object Storage platform roles: {{c1::Velero backup target}}; {{c2::Terraform state backend}}; {{c3::Loki/Tempo/Thanos chunk storage}}; {{c4::registry storage backend}}; plus CI artifacts and data exchange with on-prem.
notes.extra: Keep backup traffic cloud-local — never haul it over the virtual private network (VPN).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: What is a STACKIT Network Area (SNA)?
notes.back: An organization-level network construct: a centrally managed pool of IP ranges from which member projects get their networks, connected privately (no internet transit).
notes.analogy: STACKIT's shared VPC: the platform team owns the road network, and each project gets a plot already connected to it.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Why is the STACKIT Network Area (SNA) the hub of a hybrid STACKIT design?
notes.back: Virtual private network (VPN) and multiprotocol label switching (MPLS) connections terminate in the SNA, so on-prem routes become available to every attached project.
notes.extra: Governance: the platform team owns IP address management (IPAM) and routes centrally; project teams consume networks.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Shared STACKIT Network Area (SNA) for the whole organisation: what do you gain?
notes.back: Private project-to-project connectivity, a single hybrid hub, and central IP address management (IPAM) enforcing non-overlapping classless inter-domain routing ranges (CIDRs).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Shared STACKIT Network Area (SNA): what is the risk, and how do you compensate?
notes.back: A bigger blast radius — misrouting or compromise can propagate. Compensate with segmentation: security groups, Unified Firewall, NetworkPolicy.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: When do isolated per-project networks fit better than a shared STACKIT Network Area (SNA)?
notes.back: Fully independent tenants with no shared services or hybrid needs: hard isolation by default, and classless inter-domain routing ranges (CIDRs) may overlap.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: How do STACKIT security groups behave?
notes.back: Stateful rule sets attached to instances/interfaces; inbound is blocked until allowed; reusable across servers.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: What is the STACKIT Unified Firewall for?
notes.back: A central (beta) dashboard combining security groups, database access control lists (ACLs) and public-IP rules across projects, with templates — one policy over many projects.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: STACKIT virtual private network (VPN): protocol and supported topologies?
notes.back: Managed Internet Protocol Security (IPsec, IKEv2) gateways attached to a STACKIT Network Area (SNA); site-to-site and site-to-multisite only — no client (point-to-site) VPN.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: STACKIT virtual private network (VPN): routing options and high availability (HA) model?
notes.back: Policy-based, static or border gateway protocol (BGP) routing (BGP recommended for failover); gateways run as active-active pairs with parallel tunnels.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: STACKIT virtual private network (VPN): throughput range?
notes.back: Plans from 100 Mbit/s to 1 Gbit/s; upgrading a plan causes a brief interruption.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Managed STACKIT virtual private network (VPN) for on-prem connectivity: pros and cons?
notes.back:
+ no ops, built-in high availability (HA), border gateway protocol (BGP).
− ≤ 1 Gbit/s, Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) only, no network address translation (NAT), no client VPN, internet latency/jitter.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: When would you run self-managed virtual private network (VPN) VMs (strongSwan/WireGuard) on STACKIT instead?
notes.back: When you need network address translation (NAT), WireGuard, client VPN or unusual policies — accepting that you own high availability (HA), patching and monitoring (still over the internet).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: When is multiprotocol label switching (MPLS)/dedicated connectivity into the STACKIT Network Area (SNA) worth it?
notes.back: When bandwidth, latency guarantees or private transport (compliance) demand it — at the cost of money, carrier contracts and lead time.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Common evolution path for on-prem ↔ STACKIT connectivity?
notes.back: Start with the managed virtual private network (VPN), add multiprotocol label switching (MPLS) when demands grow, keep the VPN as backup path (border gateway protocol (BGP) handles failover).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: STACKIT Network Load Balancer vs Application Load Balancer?
notes.back:
Network Load Balancer (NLB): L4 TCP/UDP, PROXY protocol; what STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) LoadBalancer Services create.
Application Load Balancer (ALB): L7 HTTP(S), host/path/header routing, TLS termination, web application firewall (WAF) option.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Hybrid fleet: why usually run your own ingress controller behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB) rather than the managed Application Load Balancer (ALB)?
notes.back: Full feature control (canary, auth hooks, middlewares) and identical config across STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) and on-prem clusters; the ALB only saves ops for simpler setups.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: How do STACKIT DNS records get automated from Kubernetes?
notes.back: external-dns (webhook-based provider) writes records into STACKIT DNS zones pointing at ingress/load balancer (LB) IPs.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Managed PostgreSQL Flex vs an in-cluster operator: pros and cons of the managed side?
notes.back:
+ high availability (HA) plans, automated backups/patching, survives cluster rebuilds.
− version/extension lag, less tuning control, per-instance cost, network hop from pods.
notes.analogy: A serviced apartment vs owning a house: less control, but someone else fixes the boiler.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: In-cluster database (DB) operator (e.g. CloudNativePG) on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE): pros and cons?
notes.back:
+ latest versions/extensions, local latency, GitOps config, dense per-tenant packing.
− you own backup/restore, upgrades and failover testing; the DB dies with the cluster unless disaster recovery (DR) is solid.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::03 IaaS & Networking
notes.front: Heuristic: managed database (DB) or in-cluster operator on STACKIT?
notes.back: Production system of record → managed (PostgreSQL Flex). Ephemeral/dev, per-tenant micro-DBs or special extensions → operator.
notes.extra: State is the hard part of multi-cluster — managed services keep it out of the clusters.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.text: Identity planes in a hybrid STACKIT platform: {{c1::cloud control plane}} (STACKIT identity and access management (IAM) users + service accounts); {{c2::Kubernetes API}} (kubeconfigs, OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens, RBAC); {{c3::application}} (end-user single sign-on (SSO) via PingFederate); {{c4::machine}} (service accounts, K8s ServiceAccounts, CI identities, registry robots).
notes.extra: Goal: one source of truth (Active Directory (AD)) projected into all four, with joiner-mover-leaver working end to end.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Why can't Kubernetes authenticate users against Active Directory (AD)/lightweight directory access protocol (LDAP) directly, and what bridges the gap?
notes.back: kube-apiserver has no LDAP authenticator (only certs, tokens, OpenID Connect (OIDC), webhook). An OIDC provider federating to AD — PingFederate — issues ID tokens with username + group claims.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Does Kubernetes call PingFederate/Active Directory (AD) on every request?
notes.back: No. It validates the JSON Web Token (JWT) signature locally against the issuer's published keys (JSON Web Key Set (JWKS)).
notes.analogy: A bouncer checking the hologram on an ID card instead of phoning the issuing office for every guest.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: How do OpenID Connect (OIDC) claims become Kubernetes identities?
notes.back: The API server maps the username claim (e.g. email) and groups claim to a user and groups, usually with a prefix like oidc: to avoid clashes with built-ins.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Recommended RBAC design when identities come from Active Directory (AD) via OpenID Connect (OIDC)?
notes.back: Persona ClusterRoles (platform-admin, tenant-admin, developer, viewer) bound to AD groups with kind: Group, GitOps-managed fleet-wide — access becomes AD group membership.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: You may not control kube-apiserver OpenID Connect (OIDC) flags on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE). Which three designs still give PingFederate login?
notes.back: Native OIDC config if SKE exposes it (verify); Pinniped; an authenticating proxy such as kube-oidc-proxy.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: How does Pinniped work?
notes.back: One Supervisor federates to PingFederate as upstream OpenID Connect (OIDC); a Concierge per cluster exchanges Supervisor tokens for cluster credentials (TokenCredentialRequest) — no apiserver flags needed.
notes.analogy: The Supervisor is a central passport office; each cluster's Concierge is a border desk that accepts the passport and stamps a short-lived local visa.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Downside of kube-oidc-proxy in front of each API server?
notes.back: An extra hop and another critical component you operate (it impersonates users after verifying their OpenID Connect (OIDC) token).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Per-cluster OpenID Connect (OIDC) config for a fleet: pros and cons?
notes.back:
+ no extra components, native kubectl flows (kubelogin).
− N PingFederate client registrations (or one shared client), config drift risk, only where the managed offering exposes OIDC settings.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Pinniped for a fleet: pros and cons?
notes.back:
+ one upstream integration, uniform login across STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) and on-prem, short-lived certs, any conformant cluster.
− you run the Supervisor (login single point of failure (SPOF)) and Concierges; break-glass still needed.
notes.extra: Hybrid fleets with mixed cluster types usually justify Pinniped.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Do you need Dex if PingFederate already fronts Active Directory?
notes.back: No. Dex (a lightweight OpenID Connect (OIDC) broker with lightweight directory access protocol (LDAP)/security assertion markup language (SAML)/GitHub connectors) would just add a hop and ops burden.
notes.extra: Niche: an app-local broker for a component with a narrow OIDC dialect, or decoupling labs from enterprise change processes.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) break-glass when virtual private network (VPN) → PingFederate → Active Directory (AD) is down: which credentials?
notes.back: A sealed admin kubeconfig per cluster (≤ 180-day cert) in an offline/escrowed store with dual control and calendared renewal — or STACKIT CLI login by a platform owner (depends on STACKIT identity and access management (IAM), not AD).
notes.analogy: A fire axe behind glass: always there when the normal doors (SSO) fail, and it sets off an alarm when used.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: After using STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) break-glass credentials: what must you do, and what is the blast radius?
notes.back: Run SKE credential rotation — it invalidates ALL admin kubeconfigs and ServiceAccount tokens of that cluster. Alert on and audit every break-glass use.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.text: STACKIT machine auth for Terraform/CI, least → most preferred: {{c1::static service-account token}} (long-lived bearer secret, avoid) → {{c2::key flow}} (RSA key signs a JSON Web Token (JWT) exchanged for short-lived tokens; key still needs safekeeping) → {{c3::OIDC workload identity federation}} (CI job token → service account, no stored key).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Classic anti-pattern with STACKIT service accounts?
notes.back: One god-account for the whole organisation. Scope service accounts per project with least-privilege roles.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: STACKIT Secrets Manager for a hybrid platform: pro and con?
notes.back:
+ managed, cloud-local (low latency), portal/API integrated.
− another store outside your data center (DC)'s control sphere.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Central Vault/OpenBao on-prem for a hybrid platform: pro and con?
notes.back:
+ sovereign single source of truth, lightweight directory access protocol (LDAP) auth, dynamic secrets, audit.
− every cloud read crosses the virtual private network (VPN) (availability coupling), and you run it high availability (HA).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Sealed Secrets / SOPS in Git as the secrets strategy: pro and con?
notes.back:
+ GitOps-native, no runtime store.
− rotation is a commit, no dynamic secrets, key custody per cluster (Sealed Secrets) or per key management service (KMS) (SOPS).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Common hybrid answer for secrets on STACKIT?
notes.back: Central Vault as source of truth + External Secrets Operator caching into cluster Secrets (survives short link outages); SOPS only for bootstrap material.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: External Secrets Operator across a fleet: how do you limit blast radius?
notes.back: Identical ExternalSecret manifests everywhere, but each cluster has its own identity to the store, scoping what it may read.
notes.extra: External Secrets Operator (ESO) materialises native Secrets from ExternalSecrets via (Cluster)SecretStores — manifests in Git, values never.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: External Secrets Operator (ESO) failure mode when the store (e.g. on-prem Vault) is unreachable?
notes.back: Existing Secrets persist, but rotation and new secrets stall. Set sane refresh intervals and alert on sync failures.
notes.analogy: A pantry: when the supermarket (Vault) is closed you still eat from stock, but nothing new comes in.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: How are registry credentials handled across the STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) fleet?
notes.back: Pull: per-cluster/namespace robot accounts (Harbor or STACKIT Container Registry) delivered as imagePullSecrets via External Secrets Operator (ESO) or GitOps bootstrap, wired into ServiceAccounts. Push: only in CI, short-lived.
notes.extra: Image trust: sign in CI (cosign), verify in-cluster (Kyverno verifyImages) as part of the golden stack.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Role of a key management service (KMS) (STACKIT KMS or on-prem hardware security module (HSM)) in the hybrid platform?
notes.back: Envelope encryption for application data, SOPS and backups — with key sovereignty as the compliance argument.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: On STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE), which encryption is outside your control?
notes.back: etcd encryption at rest — the control plane is STACKIT's. You configure workload-level crypto, not apiserver encryption providers.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::04 Identity, Access & Secrets
notes.front: Rule for anything you back up off-platform (Velero, database (DB) dumps)?
notes.back: Encrypt it with keys you control.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.text: Tenant limits on STACKIT/STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) stack in layers: {{c1::project quotas}} (cores, RAM, volumes, public IPs; raised via support); {{c2::node pool min/max}}; {{c3::ResourceQuota}} per namespace; {{c4::LimitRange}} per pod/container (forces requests to be set).
notes.extra: Tenancy design = deciding at which of these layers a tenant is throttled.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Cluster-per-tenant on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE): pros?
notes.back: Real control-plane and node isolation, independent versions/custom resource definitions (CRDs), per-tenant blast radius and maintenance windows, clean cost attribution, offboarding = delete the cluster.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Cluster-per-tenant on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE): cons and SKE-specific mitigations?
notes.back: Per-cluster control-plane fee + baseline nodes (poor bin-packing) and fleet sprawl that demands Terraform + GitOps automation. Mitigate with hibernation for dev tenants and small autoscaling pools.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Node-level isolation for a sensitive tenant in a shared STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) cluster: how?
notes.back: A dedicated tainted node pool; tenant pods get tolerations + nodeSelector/affinity; admission policy stops other tenants tolerating it. No kernel sharing with others.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: What is the ceiling of node-pool isolation on STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE)?
notes.back: Control plane, custom resource definitions (CRDs) and upgrades stay shared, and sandboxed runtimes (gVisor/Kata) generally aren't configurable on SKE nodes — beyond that it's a separate cluster or Confidential Kubernetes.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: STACKIT project per tenant (team × env): trade-off?
notes.back:
+ hard identity and access management (IAM) boundary, own quotas, clean billing, independent service instances.
− more projects to govern → automate with Terraform landing-zone modules.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Why is a shared STACKIT project weak for tenant separation?
notes.back: Identity and access management (IAM) roles are project-wide, so separation collapses at the cloud level; plus quota contention and murky cost attribution.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Rule linking cloud-level and in-cluster tenancy boundaries?
notes.back: Cloud boundaries must be at least as strong as your strongest in-cluster boundary — no hard-isolated clusters of two tenants inside one shared project with shared identity and access management (IAM).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Why govern which tenant namespaces may egress to on-prem ranges over the virtual private network (VPN)?
notes.back: The VPN is a shared, capacity-limited link into the corporate network; NetworkPolicy egress rules should allow only tenants that need it.
notes.extra: Ship default-deny ingress+egress automatically with each tenant namespace (Capsule/GitOps template).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: GitOps/management hub on-prem: pros and cons?
notes.back:
+ in your data center (DC), direct access to Active Directory (AD)/Vault/Git.
− every reconcile crosses the virtual private network (VPN); link down = no deploys and degraded fleet visibility; sized by DC capacity.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: GitOps/management hub in STACKIT: pros and cons?
notes.back:
+ next to the fleet (fast, reliable reconciles), survives data center (DC) maintenance.
− hub credentials live in the cloud; Git unreachable = no new changes (last state keeps reconciling).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: What does "centrally managed from on-prem" really require, and what is the middle path?
notes.back: On-prem authority over Git, identity and secrets — not the hub's location. Middle path: hub in STACKIT, sources of truth on-prem, pull-based agents.
notes.analogy: Headquarters doesn't need to drive every truck; it needs to own the route plan and the keys.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.text: New STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) workload cluster, fully automated: a {{c1::Terraform module}} creates the cluster + extensions (observability, access control list (ACL)) → Terraform gets the kubeconfig and {{c2::installs the GitOps agent}}, registering the cluster with labels → {{c3::ApplicationSets match the labels}} and roll in the golden stack → {{c4::ESO pulls secrets}}, tenant apps sync and external-dns publishes records.
notes.extra: Labels: env, tier, tenant. Deletion = terraform destroy; backups and metrics survive in Object Storage and central stores.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Disaster recovery (DR) with one STACKIT region: what does in-region high availability (HA) cover?
notes.back: Node pools across eu01-1/2/3, zone-aware StatefulSets and managed databases (DBs) on HA plans — zone failures, not loss of the region or provider.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Cheapest disaster recovery (DR) option on STACKIT, and its typical recovery time objective (RTO)?
notes.back: Backup/restore: Velero to Object Storage plus database (DB) point-in-time recovery. RTO in hours.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Warm standby vs active-active disaster recovery (DR)?
notes.back:
Warm standby: second cluster with the golden stack synced but apps scaled down; restore data on failover.
Active-active: both sites serve, needing data replication + global server load balancing (GSLB) — only for the few truly critical services.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::05 Tenancy, Multi-Cluster & DR
notes.front: Why is the on-prem data center (DC) a sovereignty argument for hybrid disaster recovery (DR)?
notes.back: It doubles as an out-of-provider DR site for STACKIT workloads (and vice versa) — protection against losing the provider.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Hybrid reference topology: what stays on-prem?
notes.back: Active Directory (AD)/lightweight directory access protocol (LDAP), PingFederate, Git + CI, Vault, Harbor, central monitoring/security information and event management (SIEM), Terraform runners.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Hybrid reference topology: what lives in STACKIT?
notes.back: The STACKIT Network Area (SNA) (fed by virtual private network (VPN)/multiprotocol label switching (MPLS)), projects per team/env, STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) workload clusters (+ optional hub), managed databases (DBs), Object Storage, DNS, Observability.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: What flows over the on-prem ↔ STACKIT link, and what must not?
notes.back:
Over: GitOps pulls, auth, secret syncs, image replication, security information and event management (SIEM) telemetry, API calls.
Not over: backups, bulk data, registry pulls at scale.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Why must STACKIT Network Area (SNA) and on-prem classless inter-domain routing ranges (CIDRs) be agreed before the first project exists?
notes.back: STACKIT virtual private network (VPN) does no network address translation (NAT), so ranges must not overlap — and renumbering later is brutal.
notes.analogy: Two cities merging their street maps: if both have a "Main Street 1", mail can't be delivered without renaming streets.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: May pod/Service classless inter-domain routing ranges (CIDRs) repeat across STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) clusters?
notes.back: Yes, they're cluster-internal — unless you may later want ClusterMesh-style pod routing or pod IPs reachable from on-prem. Unique ranges keep that door open.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Besides node networks, what address space do you reserve in the STACKIT Network Area (SNA) plan?
notes.back: Load balancer (LB) IPs, virtual private network (VPN) transfer networks, a future disaster recovery (DR) site, vCluster hosts.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.text: Hybrid split-horizon DNS: {{c1::corporate zones}} stay authoritative on on-prem Active Directory (AD) DNS; {{c2::cloud zones}} live in STACKIT DNS, fed by external-dns; clusters resolve corp names via {{c3::CoreDNS stub-domain forwarders}} over the virtual private network (VPN); on-prem resolves cloud-internal names via {{c4::conditional forwarders}} on AD DNS.
notes.analogy: An internal company phonebook and a public directory: the answer depends on who is asking.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Split-horizon DNS failure mode when the virtual private network (VPN) drops?
notes.back: Corp-name resolution inside clusters fails. Tune forwarder timeouts/caching and keep cloud-local dependencies on cloud zones.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: How does on-prem tooling (Terraform, Argo CD, kubectl) reach STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) API servers — and does it need the virtual private network (VPN)?
notes.back: Over the internet: SKE API endpoints are public in STACKIT seeds (lock down with the access control list (ACL) extension). It does not depend on the VPN — good for break-glass — whereas internal load balancers (LBs) do.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: If policy forbids any public Kubernetes API exposure, what does that mean for STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE)?
notes.back: Verify current SKE private-endpoint options; if none fit, those clusters belong on-prem.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: What does authenticating via an on-prem PingFederate mean for the cloud estate?
notes.back: Every interactive login (kubectl OpenID Connect (OIDC), Argo CD single sign-on (SSO), app SSO) depends on reaching it — PingFederate becomes Tier-0 infrastructure for all STACKIT workloads.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Why do existing sessions survive a PingFederate outage while new logins fail?
notes.back: Apps validate JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) locally against cached JSON Web Key Set (JWKS); only issuing new tokens needs the identity provider (IdP).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Mitigations for the on-prem identity provider (IdP) dependency?
notes.back: Balanced token/refresh lifetimes, PingFederate high availability (HA) with redundant uplinks, break-glass paths that bypass it, and non-interactive credentials for machine traffic (GitOps, External Secrets Operator (ESO)).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Why is pulling images directly from on-prem Harbor risky for a STACKIT fleet?
notes.back: Every pull crosses the virtual private network (VPN) (capacity!), and when the link is down pods can't start on new nodes.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Preferred registry pattern for the hybrid fleet?
notes.back: Harbor push-replication to an in-region registry (STACKIT Container Registry or a Harbor in STACKIT); clusters pull locally; link outages only delay new images.
notes.analogy: Stocking a local warehouse instead of shipping every order from headquarters.
notes.extra: Always pin digests, pre-pull critical images, scan at the source and enforce signatures in-cluster.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Pull-through proxy cache in-region: drawback?
notes.back: The first pull still crosses the link, and cache eviction can bite during incidents.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: On-prem vs in-cluster STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) CI runners: trade-off?
notes.back:
On-prem: next to Git/Vault/artifacts, reach STACKIT via public APIs.
SKE: next to deploy targets and elastic — but CI becomes a noisy-neighbour tenant needing quotas.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Common split between CI builds and Terraform applies in the hybrid setup?
notes.back: Build/test in the cloud near caches; state-changing jobs (terraform apply) from a controlled on-prem runner pool using OpenID Connect (OIDC) federation to STACKIT (no stored keys).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Terraform state on STACKIT Object Storage: what is the caveat?
notes.back: Terraform ≥ 1.10 S3 lockfiles rely on conditional writes — verify the S3-compatible endpoint supports them before trusting concurrent applies.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Which STACKIT-side Terraform backend gives real locking out of the box?
notes.back: The PostgreSQL (pg) backend on PostgreSQL Flex — shown in the STACKIT provider docs as a state + locking pattern.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: On-prem GitLab HTTP backend for Terraform state: trade-off?
notes.back: State stays in the data center (DC) next to CI with existing Git auth, but GitLab becomes a dependency of every apply.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Rule for Terraform state across trust boundaries?
notes.back: Never share one state across them — split state per project/stack, since state holds secrets (kubeconfigs!).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.text: Hybrid public key infrastructure (PKI): public endpoints use {{c1::ACME/Let's Encrypt via cert-manager}} (DNS-01 against STACKIT DNS for wildcards); internal services and mutual TLS (mTLS) use a {{c2::private CA (AD CS or Vault PKI)}} as cert-manager issuer; {{c3::trust-manager}} ships the corporate root to all clusters.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) vs Vault public key infrastructure (PKI) as the internal certificate issuer?
notes.back: AD CS keeps PKI where auditors expect it but is automation-hostile; Vault PKI automates well but puts Vault on the critical path. Common: offline corporate root → Vault as issuing intermediate.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: How should 10+ STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE) clusters ship telemetry to one pane of glass?
notes.back: Per-cluster agents (Grafana Alloy / OpenTelemetry (OTel) Collector) remote-write outbound — no inbound scraping across the wide area network (WAN).
notes.analogy: Branch offices mail their reports to HQ instead of HQ phoning every branch.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Observability backend in STACKIT vs on-prem?
notes.back:
STACKIT (usually right): telemetry stays in-region, cheap and link-tolerant; on-prem users just open Grafana.
On-prem: next to the security information and event management (SIEM), but all telemetry crosses the virtual private network (VPN), with gaps on outages.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Compliance middle path for hybrid observability?
notes.back: Metrics and traces stay in-region; only filtered, audit-relevant logs are forwarded to the on-prem security information and event management (SIEM) (Telemetry Router/Alloy pipelines).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Which flows across the on-prem ↔ STACKIT link are tiny, and which are large?
notes.back:
Tiny: GitOps pulls, auth, secret sync.
Large: telemetry, image replication (bursty), backups (must not cross).

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Why is latency, not bandwidth, the killer for some cross-site flows?
notes.back: AuthN round-trips and synchronous cross-site calls add wide area network (WAN) latency to every request — keep services site-local with async replication.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: When must you move beyond the managed STACKIT virtual private network (VPN)?
notes.back: When honest demand exceeds ~1 Gbit/s sustained or needs latency guarantees → multiprotocol label switching (MPLS)/dedicated line, VPN as border gateway protocol (BGP) failover.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Hairpinning all cloud egress through on-prem inspection: trade-off?
notes.back:
+ single inspection/policy point, security information and event management (SIEM)-friendly.
− eats virtual private network (VPN) bandwidth, adds latency, and the proxy becomes a fleet-wide single point of failure (SPOF).
notes.analogy: Routing every delivery van through headquarters' inspection gate, even when the customer is next door.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Pragmatic egress design for the hybrid platform?
notes.back: Cloud-local egress with tight allow-lists (NetworkPolicy, DNS filtering, security groups) for platform traffic; hairpin only flows your compliance framework requires to be inspected.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Velero backups for STACKIT Kubernetes Engine (SKE): target, cadence — and the step people skip?
notes.back: In-region Object Storage (manifests + Container Storage Interface (CSI) snapshots), e.g. daily volumes / weekly full cluster. Regularly test restores into a scratch cluster.
notes.extra: Untested backups are hopes, not backups.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: Managed database (DB) backups on STACKIT: what to add beyond built-in backups + point-in-time recovery (PITR)?
notes.back: Logical dumps exported to Object Storage, for provider-independent copies.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: How should backup copies reach on-prem for provider-loss disaster recovery (DR)?
notes.back: Scheduled, off-peak bulk replication of the backup buckets — not over the virtual private network (VPN) plan that carries production auth traffic if volumes are large.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.front: What is your real recovery time objective (RTO) in a GitOps platform?
notes.back: The rebuild-from-scratch time: desired state from Git + secrets store + backups.
notes.analogy: A house rebuilt from blueprints (Git), a key safe (secrets) and stored furniture (backups): the rebuild time is your real recovery time.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.text: "Centrally managed from on-prem" pillars (1/2): {{c1::landing zone}} — org/folders/projects via Terraform, STACKIT Network Area (SNA) with clean IP address management (IPAM); {{c2::connectivity}} — virtual private network (VPN) or multiprotocol label switching (MPLS), non-overlapping classless inter-domain routing ranges (CIDRs); {{c3::identity}} — Active Directory (AD) → PingFederate → clusters (Pinniped/native) + Argo single sign-on (SSO), OpenID Connect (OIDC) federation for machines.
notes.extra: The VPN runs border gateway protocol (BGP) in active-active mode.

notes.deck: STACKIT Hybrid Cloud Architect::06 Hybrid & Central Management
notes.text: "Centrally managed from on-prem" pillars (2/2): {{c1::delivery}} — Git on-prem as source of truth, pull-based GitOps; {{c2::distribution}} — in-region registry replicas, secrets via central store + External Secrets Operator (ESO); {{c3::operations}} — in-region observability + security information and event management (SIEM) forwarding, backups, upgrade rings; {{c4::governance}} — tenancy per trust zone, quotas, fleet-wide policy and image signing.
notes.extra: Terraform is used for infrastructure only.
